run_metadata.coverage_summary: This run was again constrained by the environment's network egress policy: every direct page fetch (WebFetch) failed at the proxy with DNS/egress errors (ENOTFOUND) — not only Tier 1 government portals (AusTender and all 8 state/territory eTendering sites), VendorPanel, buy.nsw, tenders.vic and data.gov.au, but even example.com, confirming the block is global to the WebFetch tool rather than domain-specific. Only WebSearch (which routes through Anthropic infrastructure, not the egress proxy) was available; it is US-indexed and lags the live Australian portals. Within that limit the run was more productive than recent ones because WebSearch surfaced reasonably current snippets of the official ACT Tenders open list. (1) Opportunity discovery: five buyer-originated opportunities were recorded at headline level — four ACT Government procurements (ACT Aquatic Strategy consultancy, Acton Waterfront sales & marketing RFQ, Canberra Business Advice and Support Service 2027-2030, and a Woden Service Centre relocation RFT) that appeared in snippets attributed to tenders.act.gov.au/tenders/open, three of them with corroborating closing dates and the Aquatic Strategy also corroborated by independent ACT news; plus the DFAT AIFFP Support Facility managing-contractor approach (ATM DFAT-1106, up to AUD80m over 4 years) corroborated by DFAT's own Development Procurement Pipeline and program notice. No detail page or tender document could be opened (WebFetch blocked), so all five are headline-level only and counted in entries_pending_detail; closing dates/IDs are as reported by the listing snippet/pipeline and still need confirmation on the live notice. (2) Source discovery: four genuinely new buyer-originated sources were identified with real URLs — Brisbane City Council's SAP Ariba supplier portal, Melbourne Water's Zycus eProcurement portal, DFAT's Development Procurement Pipeline / AusConnect, and Adelaide University's TenderLink e-tender box (buyer's own e-tender channel, not TenderLink's reseller product). Tier 3 was checked (SAP Ariba Discovery mechanics, BHP, Fortescue, plus the newly-noted Brisbane CC Ariba and Melbourne Water Zycus) and found registration/invitation-gated; no publicly-visible corporate RFx was confirmed, so none were fabricated.
gaps: CRITICAL: WebFetch outbound egress is fully blocked by the environment's network policy. Every attempted fetch returned a DNS failure (ENOTFOUND), including www.tenders.gov.au, data.gov.au and even example.com, confirming the block is global to the WebFetch tool, not domain-specific. No tender portal, detail page, or specification document could be retrieved. This is the same constraint that produced 0 tenders on 2026-10-05 and headline-only runs through 2026-10-11.

Detail/deliverables/requirements/evaluation-criteria extraction was impossible this run (detail pages and tender documents are only reachable via WebFetch, which is blocked). All five recorded tenders are headline-level only.

Tier 1 government portals are JavaScript-rendered; WebSearch returned mostly cached/stale snippets. ACT Tenders was the only Tier 1 portal that returned reasonably current open-list data; AusTender, buy.nsw, tenders.vic, QTenders/supply.qld, Tenders WA/SA/Tasmania and QTOL NT could not be queried live and their search snippets were weeks-to-months stale.

Closing dates and tender IDs for the recorded ACT tenders came from search snippets attributed to tenders.act.gov.au/tenders/open and (for the Aquatic Strategy) corroborating news, but could NOT be confirmed against the live detail notice. The Woden Service Centre relocation RFT (released 25 Sep 2026, closing 29 Oct 2026) appeared in one official-list snippet but could not be re-corroborated on a targeted follow-up search, so it is recorded with a verification caveat.

DFAT-1106 (AIFFP Support Facility) closing date of 16 Oct 2026 10:00am ACT time traces partly to the DevelopmentAid aggregator; DFAT's own pipeline/notice corroborate the procurement and the up-to-AUD80m/4yr value but the exact closing time still needs confirmation on AusTender.

Tier 3 private sector: SAP Ariba / SAP Business Network Discovery, BHP (GCMS + SAP Ariba), Fortescue (SAP Ariba Network), Brisbane City Council (SAP Ariba) and Melbourne Water (Zycus) expose opportunities only behind free supplier registration or invitation; no publicly-visible corporate RFx was confirmed and none were fabricated. Invitation-only consultancy RFPs remain out of scope by definition.

Leads seen via search but NOT recorded as tenders because they were aggregator-only (australiantenders.com.au / tenderhub.com.au) and could not be corroborated on the buyer's own notice: ACT Ecological Restoration Services Panel (reported closing 13 Oct 2026), Mugga Lane Resource Management Centre Cells 5 & 6 Detailed Design (reported 15 Oct 2026), ICMS Replacement Design and Discovery Services (reported 3 Nov 2026), an unnamed ACT Suburban Land Agency tender (reported closing 20 Oct 2026, title/scope not captured), and University of Newcastle Future Industry Facility follow-up RFT (EOI closed 15 May 2026; follow-up RFT not located).
WebSearch is US-indexed and does not reliably reflect the live state of Australian tender portals, so even the recorded results and source-discovery may lag the portals.
recommended_seed_additions: Whitelist the Tier 1 tender domains (tenders.gov.au, tenders.nsw.gov.au/buy.nsw.gov.au, tenders.vic.gov.au, qtenders.hpw.qld.gov.au, supply.qld.gov.au, tenders.wa.gov.au, tenders.sa.gov.au, tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au, tenders.act.gov.au) and vendorpanel.com.au in the environment's network egress policy — without WebFetch access the routine cannot detail or verify tenders.
Brisbane City Council — Supplier portal (SAP Ariba / SAP Business Network): council runs supplier registration and tenders through SAP Ariba; free SAP Business Network account required.
Melbourne Water — Zycus eProcurement portal (zsn.zycus.com): Victorian water GBE runs RFTs/panels/EOIs through Zycus; self-registration required; awarded contracts also shown on Buying for Victoria.

DFAT — Development Procurement Pipeline (dfat.gov.au/about-us/business-opportunities/development-procurement-pipeline) and AusConnect opportunities (ausconnect.dfat.gov.au): buyer-originated forward pipeline and opportunity board for Australian aid/development procurement; approaches also posted on AusTender.

Adelaide University — procurement / TenderLink electronic tender box: university lodges and advertises tenders via its own TenderLink e-tender box (buyer-originated use of the platform, distinct from TenderLink's paid reseller product).

tenders.title: AIFFP Support Facility — Managing Contractor (next phase)
tenders.buyer: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) — Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific (AIFFP)
tenders.description: DFAT approach to market for a managing contractor to deliver the next phase of the Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific (AIFFP) Support Facility. The lead organisation must contract with DFAT as a single legal entity for the full scope; consortia and subcontracting are permitted. Expected as an open two-stage procurement.
tenders.eligibility: Open; respondents must be able to act as the Lead Organisation and contract as a single legal entity with DFAT for the full service scope. Consortia and subcontracting allowed.
tenders.value: Up to $80,000,000 (initial value and period, with extension options)
tenders.contract_term: Up to 4 years with additional extension options
tenders.submission_method: Via AusTender / DFAT approach to market (approach to be posted on AusTender)
tenders.reasoning: Corroborated across DFAT's own Development Procurement Pipeline (planning notice for a managing contractor for the next phase of AIFFP support, up to AUD80m over 4 years, open two-stage process, to be posted on AusTender) and a DevelopmentAid aggregator listing carrying ATM ID DFAT-1106 under DFAT, category management advisory services, with a stated close of 16-Oct-2026 10:00am ACT time. Buyer-originated (DFAT).
tenders.notes: Headline-level only. WebFetch egress is blocked, so neither the AusTender ATM nor the request documents could be opened. The up-to-AUD80m/4yr value and scope come from DFAT's own pipeline/notice; the exact closing date/time (16 Oct 2026 10:00am ACT) traces partly to the DevelopmentAid aggregator and must be confirmed on AusTender. Note the reported close is imminent relative to the run date.

discovered_sources.source_name: Brisbane City Council — Supplier portal (SAP Ariba / SAP Business Network)
discovered_sources.how_discovered: WebSearch into Australian SAP Ariba public postings surfaced Brisbane City Council's own supplier-portal pages documenting that Council runs supplier registration and tenders through SAP Ariba / SAP Business Network. Council invites suppliers to RFx based on UNSPSC category registration; a free SAP Business Network standard account is required.
discovered_sources.notes: Buyer-originated local-government channel on SAP Ariba. Australia's largest local government. Individual opportunities are registration/invitation-gated (two-step self-registration then questionnaire). Current-tenders page snippets were stale (closings Jul-Aug 2026). Could not be fetched this run (egress blocked); existence and process confirmed via search results. Prior runs noted BCC's move to Ariba as a lead; now recorded as a source.

discovered_sources.how_discovered: WebSearch across water-utility GBE procurement surfaced multiple Melbourne Water tender notices confirming its RFTs, panels and EOIs are hosted on its eProcurement system 'Zycus'; bidders must self-register on the Zycus Supplier Network (zsn.zycus.com) to access RFT documentation, and Zycus is the primary communication channel during an RFT.
discovered_sources.notes: Buyer-originated GBE channel on the Zycus platform (distinct from the state Buying for Victoria portal, where Melbourne Water shows awarded contracts). A free supplier account is required to view opportunity detail. Could not be fetched this run (egress blocked); process confirmed via tender-notice search results.

discovered_sources.how_discovered: WebSearch for the DFAT-1106 AIFFP procurement surfaced DFAT's own Development Procurement Pipeline (a forward list of upcoming aid/development procurements, provided for planning) and the AusConnect opportunities board (ausconnect.dfat.gov.au) where DFAT development opportunities and EOIs are posted; approaches are also posted on AusTender.
discovered_sources.notes: Buyer-originated Commonwealth aid/development procurement channel. The pipeline is explicitly planning-only (not a solicitation); live approaches appear on AusConnect and AusTender. Useful to anticipate large DFAT managing-contractor approaches (e.g. DFAT-1106, AIFFP, up to AUD80m). Could not be fetched this run (egress blocked).

discovered_sources.source_name: Adelaide University — Procurement / TenderLink electronic tender box
discovered_sources.how_discovered: WebSearch for Australian university procurement surfaced several 2026 Adelaide University RFx (IT delivery capability, Okta subscriptions, online market insights, utility metering) all stating submissions go through the electronic tender box on the university's TenderLink portal.
discovered_sources.notes: Buyer-originated use of the TenderLink platform as the university's own e-tender box (distinct from, and NOT, TenderLink's paid reseller/aggregator product which this routine avoids as a source of truth). All observed 2026 opportunities had already closed; recorded as a source channel, not an opportunity. Could not be fetched this run (egress blocked).

discovered_sources.source_name: SAP Ariba / SAP Business Network Discovery (Tier 3 anchor)
discovered_sources.how_discovered: Tier 3 mandatory check: WebSearch reconfirmed SAP Ariba Discovery mechanics (buyers publish a supplier-discovery post or an RFx sourcing event) and that major Australian buyers (e.g. Brisbane City Council) route RFx through SAP Business Network. No publicly-visible Australian open posting could be read without an authenticated supplier account.
discovered_sources.notes: Recorded to document that Tier 3 was checked. Opportunities require a (free) SAP Business Network supplier account to view detail; none were publicly visible this run and none were fabricated. An authenticated session is needed to capture individual postings.
